content: Furosemide, commonly referred to as a water pill, is prescribed to alleviate swelling and fluid retention caused by various medical conditions, such as heart or liver disease. It is also used to manage high blood pressure. This medication works by prompting the kidneys to excrete excess water and salt into the urine. In some cases, furosemide may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Furosemide is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken once daily in the morning or twice daily in the morning and afternoon. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist to clarify any part you do not understand. Take furosemide exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. While furosemide helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure it. Continue taking furosemide even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking furosemide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to furosemide, sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Additionally, disclose all other medications you are taking, including corticosteroids (e.g., prednisone), digoxin (Lanoxin), indomethacin (Indocin), lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid), diabetes medications, probenecid (Benemid), and vitamins. If you are also taking cholestyramine or colestipol, take these at least one hour after taking furosemide. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had diabetes, gout, or kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. If you become pregnant while on furosemide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking furosemide. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as furosemide may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Follow your doctor’s dietary instructions while taking furosemide. Your doctor may recommend consuming potassium-rich foods, such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice, to counteract potential potassium loss. If you miss a dose of furosemide, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Frequent urination may occur for up to six hours after taking a dose of furosemide, but this should decrease after a few weeks of use. Notify your doctor if you experience severe or persistent symptoms such as muscle cramps, weakness, dizziness, confusion, thirst, upset stomach, vomiting, blurred vision, headache, restlessness, or constipation. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: fever, sore throat, ringing in the ears, unusual bleeding or bruising, hearing loss, severe rash with peeling skin, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or rapid, excessive weight loss. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store furosemide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Discard any unused furosemide liquid after 60 days. Dispose of outdated or no longer needed medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular monitoring. Your blood pressure should be checked regularly, and occasional blood tests may be required. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
